summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of gold's role in a portfolio, particularly for Indian investors, with correct details on Sovereign Gold Bonds.

claims.claim: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) are issued by the Reserve Bank of India on behalf of the Government of India.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm SGBs are issued by RBI on behalf of the Government of India.

claims.claim: They offer an annual interest rate (currently 2.50% per annum)
claims.note: The interest rate for SGBs is indeed 2.50% per annum, paid semi-annually.

claims.claim: capital gains arising on redemption to an individual are exempt from tax.
claims.note: Capital gains on redemption of SGBs for individuals are exempt from tax. However, some sources indicate that from April 1, 2026, this exemption will apply only to original subscribers who hold the bonds until maturity.

claims.claim: SGBs do not get any indexation benefit, as they were completely removed in Union Budget 2024.
claims.note: RBI and other sources state that indexation benefits are provided to long-term capital gains arising to any person on transfer of the bond. The claim about removal in Union Budget 2024 is not supported by authoritative sources.

claims.claim: If you sell your SGBs before maturity, capital gains tax applies. Held for more than 1 year: You pay long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax, at 12.5% (without indexation).
claims.note: LTCG on transfer of SGBs is taxed at 20% with indexation benefit if held for more than 12 months. The 12.5% rate is incorrect, and indexation benefit is available.

article_title: Gold's Resilience: Geopolitics, Inflation, and Your Portfolio
